intended_use.statement: Evaluate supervisory pump-scheduling candidates against a deterministic digital twin for commissioning support, operator training, sequence review, and machine-native assurance research.
exclusions: Direct connection to live pumps, valves, PLC outputs, or SCADA write interfaces.
Use as a hydraulic design model, treatment-process model, regulatory compliance system, or autonomous production controller.
Use where a failed simulation result could itself create a physical consequence.

inputs: Timestamped tank-level percentage, observed demand estimate, power availability, and telemetry quality.
Actual digital-twin demand, which may differ from the planner-visible demand estimate in model-error scenarios.
Bounded plant configuration and pump characteristics.
Controller checkpoint containing command state, sequence, dwell timers, and journal tail identity.
outputs: Expiring, monotonically sequenced duty and standby pump intent records.
Original planner proposal states, safety disposition, adjudication mode, and reasons.
Hash-chained audit journal entries and deterministic scenario evidence.
Per-scenario terminal-inventory-normalized comparisons and safety-kernel intervention statistics.
state: Last authorized pump states and transition times.
Last intent sequence and journal tail hash.
Digital-twin tank volume, pump starts, energy proxy, unmet demand, and overflow.
state_transitions: Planner proposal is always adjudicated by the readable safety kernel before journaling.
Journal sequence advances exactly once for each decision step.
Checkpoint restoration must preserve controller sequence and journal continuity.
Rejected corrupted checkpoint probes cannot alter live plant or controller state.
Digital-twin state advances only from an authorized, non-expired intent and actual scenario inputs.

observable: Authorized pump intents, original proposals, safety dispositions, modes, reasons, sequence numbers, expiration times, and journal hashes.
Scenario-level initial and final storage, energy proxy, starts, unmet demand, overflow, corruption rejection, and invariant violations.
Inventory-adjusted energy, terminal reserve delta, pump-start regression, and all per-scenario gate outcomes.
Deterministic reproduction of the same results from the same identified inputs.
errors: Malformed or digest-invalid checkpoints are rejected.
Non-monotonic or skipped journal sequences are rejected.
Planner identity mismatch during restoration is rejected.
malformed_inputs: Non-finite, negative-demand, or out-of-range level telemetry produces HOLD without a command change.
Unknown checkpoint structure or missing required fields is rejected.
A scenario with no actual demand value for a step is rejected.
adversarial_inputs: Stale, conflicting, replayed, reordered, or corrupted state and telemetry inputs.
Concurrent power outage and stale telemetry, restart during degraded telemetry, near-empty storage, and repeated checkpoint corruption.
Planner-visible demand estimates that understate or overstate actual digital-twin demand.
Planner proposals that enable standby without duty or request operation at high-high level.
Artifact substitution through a checkpoint carrying a different planner identity.
external_effects: Development code writes only local JSON evidence and optional local checkpoint files.
The case study emits no industrial protocol traffic and has no actuator interface.

resource: One tank, one duty pump, one standby pump, and bounded in-memory state.
The generated planner table has a fixed 7 x 3 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 3 state space.
No dynamic plugin loading, network access, or unbounded event retention is required.
timing: Telemetry older than 180 simulated seconds cannot change a command.
Authorized intents expire 120 simulated seconds after issuance.
Normal transitions honor 600-second minimum on-time and 300-second minimum off-time.

safety: No pump may be authorized at or above the declared high-high level.
Both pumps are authorized during a valid low-low emergency while power is available.
Standby cannot be authorized without duty.
Bad or stale telemetry cannot change the previously authorized command.
Loss of power produces an all-off intent.
Normal planner requests cannot bypass minimum dwell times.
security: Intent sequences advance exactly once and replay is rejected.
Every journal entry binds the previous hash and complete authorized intent, including the original proposal and safety disposition.
Checkpoint payloads are digest protected and bind the planner identity.
Every injected checkpoint corruption is rejected without changing live state.
The planner has no direct actuator, journal, or checkpoint write authority.

environment: Python 3.11 or newer with deterministic integer and rounded IEEE-754 floating-point evidence behavior used by the test environment.
Repository-local source, generated table, contract, scenarios, thresholds, and preregistration are treated as identified inputs.
Development CI includes fresh GitHub-hosted x64 and ARM64 virtual machines.
The digital twin uses fixed-step simulation and does not model water quality, pressure zones, pipe transients, or equipment curves.
compatibility: Development scenarios and evidence format version 0.2.
Planner replacements must preserve the Planner protocol and receive a new identity.
EdgeStream integration is isolated behind a separately evidenced telemetry adapter.

implementation_defined: Floating-point formatting beyond the six decimal places retained in scenario evidence.
Filesystem durability guarantees below the atomic rename boundary.
excluded: Behavior under live field I/O, real PLC scan timing, real sensor calibration failure, and hydraulic transients.
Simultaneous multi-process writers to one checkpoint path.
Operator authentication, industrial network security, and regulatory control requirements.

limitations: The reference is a deterministic software model, not an independently calibrated physical system.
Repository-visible scenarios cannot serve as an independent final holdout.
The protected-at-execution campaign hides exact runtime scenarios until the candidate and evaluator are committed, but the evaluator authority remains the repository owner.
tolerances: Scenario evidence rounds continuous quantities to six decimal places.
Safety invariants, sequence values, starts, corruption counts, and journal identities require exact agreement.
Terminal inventory normalization uses the declared duty-pump marginal energy per stored liter.

ambiguities: A domain reviewer has not yet determined whether the low-low response should always start both pumps for every real installation.
Energy and inventory-normalized values are development proxies and do not include pump curves, motor efficiency, demand charges, or generator loading.
The operational criticality mapping for a future real deployment remains unresolved.

versioning.material_change_rule: Any change to authority boundaries, safety thresholds, telemetry semantics, plant topology, intent lifetime, checkpoint meaning, output evidence semantics, or objective thresholds creates a new contract identity.

findings.summary: The contract has not received independent water-utility, controls, or safety review.
Cross-host protected-at-execution development evaluation is automated, but no independently controlled final holdout exists.

limitations: Contract status remains UNKNOWN until independent adequacy and domain review are completed.
Passing development tests does not authorize production use or establish a safety integrity level.
